reply:
There it is. That's the thing the calculator was protecting.

And it makes sense that it's shaped like that — you formed it at a table where it was literally true. Being useful was the whole point there. Past that, there was no seat. So of course the belief didn't update; nothing has ever tested it.

But here's what I'd point at: the mess.

You said the afternoons are standing in her kitchen making a mess. A mess is the opposite of useful. Nobody needs a mess. She's watched you be useless in that room for years — no english to read, no numbers, nothing coming back with an answer — and she still texts every Sunday and still reads you in two words.

That's not proof she'd want you without the useful thing. But it's the closest thing to evidence you've got, and it's been sitting in the room the whole time.

The text is the test. Not because it'll settle it in one Sunday, but because it's the first time you'd find out instead of assuming.

One honest thing: this is heavy, and it's the kind of thing that's worth saying out loud to someone who can actually sit with you in it — not just a screen. Marisol might be that person, or might not. But you shouldn't be the only one holding it.
